title: OOM hedging and KV-journal reconciliation playbook for cross-environment memory turbulence
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Summary: A recurring class of production incidents across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private clusters has caused GPU OOM cascades in the face of KV-cache metadata inconsistencies and ephemeral arena fragmentation. Customers observe sudden tail-latency spikes and instance evictions when tenant workloads hit a pathological allocation pattern (long sessions + heavy prefix caching). This ticket contains a reproducible triage, short-term mitigations, and a runtime patch plan (journal reconciliation + hedging guardrails) intended to prevent OOM cascades while we stabilize compaction behavior.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-lived session workload that performs repeated prefix-heavy generation with cacheable KV entries; 2) Rapidly scale concurrent sessions from 10->200 on a single node; 3) Interleave large single-shot requests that bypass batching and allocate transient tensors; 4) Observe gradual slab saturation, KV-journal metadata divergence (missing tombstones) and then abrupt GPU OOMs within 3-7 minutes. Seen on both Ampere and Hopper VMs with quantized models under sequence length 2048 loads.
mitigation_actions: 1) Immediate customer-facing throttles: enable per-tenant request concurrency cap and short-circuit large single-shot requests via rate-limit headers (rolled to hosted control plane)
2) Emergency runtime config: enable 'oom_hedge' knob which enforces ephemeral_arena_soft_cap and triggers cooperative eviction earlier (deployed as an env flag)
3) Live KV-journal repair: run reconciler that scans journal segments and applies tombstone reconciliation for known corrupted ranges (run on affected nodes only)
4) Node restart guidance: for nodes with >80% slab fragmentation, recommend rolling restart with warm-cache priming to avoid coldstart spike
proposed_fix: Implement a two-part runtime patch: A) Journal reconciliation routine that replays and compacts KV-journal segments into a canonical index, healing missing tombstones and restoring accurate free lists; B) OOM hedging layer that applies tenant-aware soft caps, adaptive preemptive eviction, and a lightweight allocation sampler to detect slab hotspots and throttle allocations from noisy tenants. The patch will include runtime metrics and provenance tags to allow safe rollback.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit/integration on staging with stress harness (72h soak) -> 2) Canary on 3 low-traffic pods in hosted US-WEST-2 -> 3) Canary on two Dedicated pools with empty customers -> 4) Gradual ramp to 20% traffic with automatic fallbacks to previous allocator path if error rate rises >1% or latency SLO regresses >10% -> 5) Full rollout across regions in runtime-1.22. Each stage gated by metrics in the dashboard link below and a mandatory on-call approval.
test_plan: - Add deterministic KV-journal corruption tests to unit suite. - Integration stress: multi-tenant workload generator that simulates long sessions and mix of tiny+giant requests. - Chaos tests: node OOM injection and simulated journal segment loss to validate reconciler idempotency. - Perf: benchmark allocator latency and end-to-end P95 token latency before/after patch.
monitoring: New dashboards: 'oom_hedge/alloc_backpressure', 'kv_journal/reconciler_success', 'slab_fragmentation/percent', and alert rules: 'oom_hedge_triggered (>1/min)', 'journal_reconcile_failures (>0 in 10m)', 'slab_fragmentation > 70%'. Hook alert actions to runbook that includes immediate throttle, reconciler invocation, and paged on-call.
postmortem_actions: 1) Run full inventory of nodes impacted during the Feb incidents and upload sanitized traces to the incident archive.
2) Formalize KV-journal schema versioning and add forward/backward compatibility checks in runtime startup.
3) Add tenant isolation quotas that prevent noisy-tenant amplification across affinity groups.
4) Schedule a cross-team design review with storage and scheduler to discuss long-term compaction improvements (Q2 goal).
